ic_name: MIPI DSI v1.01.00 (Display Serial Interface, MIPI Alliance)

protocol_overview.type: Packet-based half-duplex bidirectional serial display interface on top of source-synchronous DDR D-PHY physical layer; combines DPI-2 pixel streaming (Video Mode) and DBI-2-style command/parameter transport (Command Mode) into one serialized link.
protocol_overview.duplex: Half-duplex per Data Lane 0 (the only bidirectional lane); additional Data Lanes 1..3 are strictly unidirectional host → peripheral.
wire_names: Data0+ / Data0- (Data Lane 0 — bidirectional in LP)
protocol_overview.dual_mode_signaling: HS (high-speed differential 100-200 mV terminated) + LP (low-power 1.2 V single-ended) on the same Dp/Dn pair; mode arbitrated by the lane-state controller.
protocol_overview.DDR_clock: Source-synchronous DDR Clock Lane — both edges latch one bit per Data Lane; data-rate-per-lane = 2 × Clock-Lane Hz. Clock Lane is host → peripheral only (never reversed).
protocol_overview.controller_role: Host processor: drives Clock Lane; transmits all forward-direction HS / LP packets; initiates BTA; programs T_INIT_MASTER ≥ t_POR + T_INIT_SLAVE + T_INTERNAL_DELAY at power-up.
protocol_overview.target_role: Peripheral (display module): receives forward HS / LP packets; after BTA, transmits LP reverse-direction packets (Acknowledge, Acknowledge and Error Report, Read Response, Tearing Effect trigger message); returns bus to host with its own BTA.

functional_requirements.text: DSI peripherals shall support either Command Mode (DCS commands + frame buffer at peripheral) or Video Mode (real-time pixel streaming from host), or both.

Host shall implement at minimum 1 Data Lane plus 1 Clock Lane; additional Data Lanes 1..3 are optional. Host with N-Lane capability shall be capable of operating with any number of Lanes from 1 to N to interoperate with peripherals having M ≤ N Lanes.
Clock Lane shall be driven by the host processor only, never by the peripheral. Continuous Clock Mode shall be supported by all DSI transmitters and receivers; Non-Continuous Clock Mode is optional.
In a Command Mode system, Data Lane 0 shall be bidirectional; additional Data Lanes shall be unidirectional. In a Video Mode system, Data Lane 0 may be bidirectional or unidirectional.
Forward-direction Low Power transmissions shall use Data Lane 0 only. Reverse-direction (peripheral → host) transmissions shall use Low Power Mode only and shall use Data Lane 0 only.

DSI shall transport data using two packet structures: Short Packet = 4 bytes (DI + Data0 + Data1 + ECC); Long Packet = 6..65541 bytes (DI + Word Count LS + Word Count MS + ECC + WC payload bytes + 2-byte Checksum).
Data Identifier byte DI[7:0] = VC[7:6] (Virtual Channel, 4 channels) + DT[5:0] (Data Type). DI is always the first byte of every packet.

Every Packet Header shall carry an 8-bit ECC that provides single-bit error correction + 2-bit error detection over the 24 data bits (DI + WC) using a Hamming-modified code. P6 and P7 of the ECC byte are unused and shall be 0 by transmitter; receiver shall ignore P6/P7 and force them to 0 before processing.

Long Packet Payload Checksum shall be a 16-bit CRC with generator polynomial x^16 + x^12 + x^5 + 1, initial value 0xFFFF, LSB-first shift. Checksum covers payload bytes only; for zero-length payload the Checksum shall be 0xFFFF. If peripheral does not calculate Checksum, it shall transmit 0x0000.
All packet data traverses the interface as bytes, LSB-first within each byte; multi-byte fields (WC, Checksum) traverse least-significant-byte-first unless otherwise specified.

Devices compliant with DSI v1.01 shall support EoTp Short Packet (DT = 0x08, VC = 0, payload = 0x0F0F, ECC = 0x01) generation and detection. EoTp shall be sent at the end of every HS transmission when EoTp is enabled, and shall NOT be sent for LP transmissions. Devices shall provide a means to enable / disable EoTp for interoperability with DSI v1.0 peripherals.

Bus Turn-Around (BTA) shall use the LP Escape Mode mechanism defined in the D-PHY specification. After a Read Request or any command that expects a peripheral response, the host shall assert TurnRequest to its PHY, which issues the BTA sequence. After the peripheral transmits its response, the peripheral shall return bus control to the host via its own TurnRequest.

In a bidirectional Link, the peripheral shall respond with one or more appropriate packets after every host transmission that asserts BTA, then return bus ownership to the host. If BTA is not asserted, the peripheral shall NOT communicate an Acknowledge or error information back to the host.

Up to four Virtual Channels (VC[1:0]) shall be supported; this specification only normatively addresses connection of a host to a single peripheral, but the VC field permits multi-peripheral implementations beyond the scope of this document.

Peripheral shall implement ECC checking; implementing Checksum checking is optional. Peripheral shall report errors via Acknowledge and Error Report Short Packet (peripheral-sourced DT = 0x02) after BTA — see L17/L15 for the 16-bit Error Report bit definitions.

Bidirectional peripheral shall implement HRX_TO (HS RX Timeout) and LTX-P_TO (LP TX Peripheral Timeout). Host shall implement HTX_TO (HS TX Timeout) and LRX-H_TO (LP RX Host Timeout). LRX-H_TO must be set longer than LTX-P_TO so the peripheral has returned to LP-RX before host LP-RX timer expires.

After power-on the host shall drive sustained LP-11 TX-Stop on all Lanes for at least T_INIT. The peripheral shall power up in RX-Stop and ignore all Link states for at least T_INIT. The host's T_INIT_MASTER shall be ≥ t_POR + T_INIT_SLAVE + T_INTERNAL_DELAY of the peripheral.

When N_data_lanes > 1, Lane Distributor shall send packet bytes round-robin (byte k → lane (k mod N)); all Lanes shall start SoT in parallel; if total byte count is not an integer multiple of N some Lanes may complete EoT one byte earlier than others. All Lanes shall use a single common Clock Lane.

Tearing Effect (TE) reporting from a Command Mode display module shall be transmitted as the LP Escape Mode trigger message byte 0x5D (LSB-first 10111010); the host shall first give bus possession to the peripheral via BTA without an accompanying DSI command, and shall return bus possession to itself after TE arrives or its TE-wait timeout expires.

Video Mode peripherals shall support at least one of three packet sequences: Non-Burst with Sync Pulses (transmits both Sync Start and Sync End events with packet width matching DPI timing), Non-Burst with Sync Events (only Sync Start), Burst Mode (RGB packets time-compressed).

Command Mode peripherals shall support the Display Command Set (DCS) as the standardized command transport. DCS Short Write 0/1 param (0x05/0x15), DCS Read no-param (0x06), DCS Long Write / write_LUT (0x39), DCS Short Read Response 1/2 byte (0x21/0x22), and DCS Long Read Response (0x1C) shall be implementable on top of DSI Short/Long Packets.

Video Mode host processors shall implement all four pixel formats: 16-bpp RGB565 (DT=0x0E), 18-bpp RGB666 Packed (DT=0x1E), 18-bpp RGB666 Loosely Packed (DT=0x2E), and 24-bpp RGB888 (DT=0x3E). Video Mode peripherals shall implement at least one of these formats.

During a power-on or Reset sequence, the peripheral's Maximum Return Packet Size shall be set to a default value of one. The host shall use Set Maximum Return Packet Size (DT=0x37) Short Packet to program the desired value before issuing READ commands. This Short Packet shall be ignored by peripherals with unidirectional DSI interfaces.

Data Type codes with four LSBs = 0b0000 or 0b1111 shall NOT be used (DO NOT USE class). All other unspecified codes are Reserved. DT encoding ensures at least one 0-1 or 1-0 transition in DT[3:0], aiding packet-boundary discovery via bit-level transitions.

configurations.name: Command Mode + 1 Lane (bidir)
configurations.description: Smallest bidirectional config: 1 Clock Lane + 1 bidirectional Data Lane 0. Supports DCS read/write and Tearing Effect.

configurations.name: Command Mode + 2..4 Lanes
configurations.description: Data Lane 0 bidirectional + 1..3 additional unidirectional Data Lanes for higher write bandwidth; reads still constrained to Data Lane 0.

configurations.name: Video Mode + 1..4 Lanes, unidirectional
configurations.description: Cost-optimized Video Mode display without on-panel buffer; all Data Lanes unidirectional host → peripheral; no read-back or error reporting.

configurations.name: Video Mode + 1..4 Lanes, bidirectional
configurations.description: Video Mode with bidirectional Data Lane 0 to allow Acknowledge and Error Report and limited DCS commands.

configurations.name: Continuous Clock Mode
configurations.description: Clock Lane stays in HS forever; Data Lanes alternate HS/LP per burst — lowest latency.

configurations.name: Non-Continuous Clock Mode
configurations.description: Clock Lane returns to LP-11 between HS bursts — saves clock-tree power.

configurations.name: EoTp enabled
configurations.description: Every HS transmission ends with EoTp Short Packet (DT=0x08, payload 0x0F0F) — most robust end-of-HS detection.

configurations.name: EoTp disabled
configurations.description: Backward-compatible with v1.0 peripherals; HS end is signaled only by D-PHY EoT sequence.

error_response_conditions: ECC single-bit error — corrected; peripheral may set ECC Single Bit (bit 8) in next Error Report.
ECC multi-bit error — packet dropped; bit 9 ECC Multi Bit set in next Error Report; rest of transmission also dropped.
Checksum mismatch on Long Packet payload — bit 10 Checksum Error set; payload still consumed per WC.
Unrecognized Data Type — bit 11 DSI DT Not Recognized set; receiver loses packet boundary in the rest of the transmission.
Invalid VC ID — bit 12 DSI VC ID Invalid set.
Invalid Transmission Length — bit 13 set when bytes received do not match WC field.
DSI Protocol Violation — bit 15 set, e.g. expected EoTp not received or expected BTA not received after read request.
SoT Error — bit 0 set (PHY-detected start-of-transmission corrupted).
Escape Mode Entry Command Error — bit 3 set.
Low-Power Transmit Sync Error — bit 4 set.
HS Receive Timeout Error — bit 5 set (HRX_TO expired).
LP Contention — both endpoints drive conflicting LP states; detection per Annex A Cases 1/2/3.
compliance_requirements: Sync pattern, HS Entry / Exit sequences, and lane-state encoding inherit unchanged from MIPI D-PHY v0.90.00.
Packet Header ECC = Hamming-modified single-bit-correct / 2-bit-detect over 24-bit DI + WC.
Long-Packet Payload Checksum = 16-bit CRC, polynomial x^16+x^12+x^5+1, init 0xFFFF, LSB-first; zero-byte payload Checksum = 0xFFFF; peripheral without checksum capability transmits 0x0000.
All DSI transmitters and receivers shall support Continuous Clock behavior on the Clock Lane.
Host LP clock frequency shall be in the range 67%..150% of peripheral LP clock frequency (3:2 ratio cap).

All Long packets containing pixel data shall have payload length WC that is a multiple of bytes; pixel formats further constrain payload length (e.g. 18-bpp packed must be multiple of nine bytes / four pixels).
Set Maximum Return Packet Size (0x37) default value at power-on or reset shall be 1.
Reserved bit positions in the Error Report (bits 7 and 14) shall be sent as 0.
